Dina: Ran a 2h long-context replay across Hosted / Dedicated / Private (on-prem) to repro persistent RSS growth in the KV cache. TL;DR: behavior diverges between envs, looks like config + kernel choice + batching heuristics interacting.
Mike: Can you paste the profiling output? short snippets fine.
Dina: Pasting a tiny excerpt from perf-agent:
```
-- Hosted (prod-us): RSS_MB: 420 -> 430 -> 431 (flat after 80k tokens)
-- Dedicated (reserved): RSS_MB: 410 -> 480 -> 560 (steady climb)
-- Private (onprem): RSS_MB: 395 -> 720 -> OOM-ish >900 (after ~120k tokens)
kv_evictions: Hosted=low, Dedicated=high, Private=extreme
kernel: Hosted=optimized_attn_xla, Dedicated=fallback_generic, Private=fallback_generic_fast
```
Dina: Note: Dedicated was running with old kv_slot_reserve=0.02, Hosted had 0.12; onprem has hugepages disabled.
Sara: That config drift on kv_slot_reserve would explain Dedicated eviction spikes. Also fallback kernel on Dedicated/Private likely increases per-frame allocations and fragmentation.
Oliver: For onprem, hugepages off + smaller MTU on customer infra means more page churn and smaller allocations -> fragmentation. Did you check jemalloc arena stats?
Dina: Yep, small snapshot: `arenas: active=12, dirty_pages=18%, retained=120MB` — fragmentation up on Private.
Mike: Two actionable ideas: 1) Align kv_slot_reserve across fleets to 0.10 for parity. 2) Force kernel-selection table to prefer optimized_attn_xla for Dedicated if GPU arch matches (temp toggle) to confirm kernel impact.
Oliver: Also try enabling hugepages or set MALLOC_CONF to reduce arena growth on onprem, and run a short repro with batching heuristics turned to "conservative" (smaller batch size) to see if continuous batching is causing cache growth.
Dina: I repro'd with conservative batching and saw Dedicated RSS climb flatten earlier (~560 -> 565 -> stable). Private still noisy but much slower.
infra-bot: Deployment note: will roll kv_slot_reserve config to dedicated pool tomorrow 03:30 UTC.
Dina: Opening an ENG-RUNTIME issue with logs, perf slices, and a short repro script. Assigning to @Oliver and @Mike for kernel + jemalloc follow-ups.
Mike: Thanks. If we confirm kernel is the main amplifier we should ship a kernel-selection guardrail to avoid generic fallbacks on production fleets.
Sara: Also add an eval run to Redwood Optimize that tracks long-context KV residency over token horizons so regressions catch this early.
Dina: Agreed. I'll include checklist in the issue (config align, kernel gate, malloc tuning, long-context eval)
